sections.heading: 1. FY2025 Spend and Performance Overview
sections.body: Total FY2025 IT Services spend closed at $48.7M, representing a 9.4% increase over FY2024 driven primarily by cloud migration support and application modernization projects. Spend was fragmented across 27 suppliers, with the top five accounting for 62% of total outlay. Supplier scorecards indicate material performance variance: three vendors achieved SLA adherence above 98%, while eight fell below the 95% threshold, particularly in incident resolution and project milestone predictability. This fragmentation has limited leverage in rate negotiations and increased administrative overhead across Procurement and IT.

sections.heading: 2. Category Segmentation and Make-versus-Buy Analysis
sections.body: The category has been segmented into four sub-towers: Infrastructure Managed Services, Application Development & Maintenance (ADM), Cybersecurity Operations, and IT Project Augmentation. A structured make-versus-buy assessment determined that core cybersecurity monitoring (Tier 1 SOC) should transition in-house by Q3 FY2026 due to recurring annual external spend of $3.8M and stable workload patterns. Conversely, ADM for legacy ERP and niche cloud engineering will remain outsourced given limited internal capacity and the high cost of specialist recruitment. The resulting hybrid model is projected to reduce steady-state run-rate costs by 6–8% while improving control over critical security functions.

sections.heading: 3. Preferred Supplier Panel Design
sections.body: We propose consolidating from 27 suppliers to a panel of 8 preferred partners structured by service tower. Selection criteria include demonstrated delivery performance (minimum 97% SLA compliance), rate competitiveness benchmarked against Gartner 2025 indices, financial stability (minimum BBB equivalent), and proven data protection controls aligned to ISO 27001. Incumbents NexaCore Solutions, BrightMile Technologies, and Orion Digital Services are recommended for panel inclusion based on superior quality metrics and cooperative pricing behavior during Q2 renegotiations. Panelization is expected to concentrate 85% of FY2026 spend within contracted rate cards and standardized terms.

sections.heading: 4. Contracting Approach and Commercial Levers
sections.body: All panel suppliers will operate under a unified Master Services Agreement (MSA) with harmonized liability caps, audit rights, and cybersecurity clauses. Rate cards will shift from time-and-materials dominance (currently 71% of spend) toward milestone-based and outcome-based pricing for project work, targeting a 12% reduction in blended day rates. Volume rebates of 2–4% will be triggered once annualized spend exceeds predefined thresholds per supplier. Additionally, gainshare provisions will be embedded in infrastructure optimization engagements to incentivize measurable cost take-out.

sections.heading: 5. FY2026 Savings and Risk Control Targets
sections.body: The combined impact of supplier consolidation, internalization of Tier 1 SOC, and revised commercial constructs is forecast to deliver $4.1M in gross savings by the end of FY2026, equating to 8.4% of the current baseline. Risk exposure will be reduced through standardized data protection addenda, mandatory quarterly business reviews, and enhanced performance credit mechanisms tied to critical SLAs. Procurement and IT will jointly monitor savings realization via a quarterly benefits tracker reported to the Executive Finance Committee. Implementation of the preferred panel is scheduled to commence January 2026 with full transition by September 2026.

structure.full_text:
IT Services Category Rationalization and Contracting Strategy – FY2025 Baseline to FY2026 Targets
Ref: SS-IT-25-184 | Date: 22 October 2025 | From: Director, Strategic Sourcing | To: CFO and CIO

Section 1. FY2025 Spend and Performance Overview
Total FY2025 IT Services spend closed at $48.7M, representing a 9.4% increase over FY2024 driven primarily by cloud migration support and application modernization projects. Spend was fragmented across 27 suppliers, with the top five accounting for 62% of total outlay. Supplier scorecards indicate material performance variance: three vendors achieved SLA adherence above 98%, while eight fell below the 95% threshold, particularly in incident resolution and project milestone predictability. This fragmentation has limited leverage in rate negotiations and increased administrative overhead across Procurement and IT.

Section 2. Category Segmentation and Make-versus-Buy Analysis
The category has been segmented into four sub-towers: Infrastructure Managed Services, Application Development & Maintenance (ADM), Cybersecurity Operations, and IT Project Augmentation. A structured make-versus-buy assessment determined that core cybersecurity monitoring (Tier 1 SOC) should transition in-house by Q3 FY2026 due to recurring annual external spend of $3.8M and stable workload patterns. Conversely, ADM for legacy ERP and niche cloud engineering will remain outsourced given limited internal capacity and the high cost of specialist recruitment. The resulting hybrid model is projected to reduce steady-state run-rate costs by 6–8% while improving control over critical security functions.

Section 3. Preferred Supplier Panel Design
We propose consolidating from 27 suppliers to a panel of 8 preferred partners structured by service tower. Selection criteria include demonstrated delivery performance (minimum 97% SLA compliance), rate competitiveness benchmarked against Gartner 2025 indices, financial stability (minimum BBB equivalent), and proven data protection controls aligned to ISO 27001. Incumbents NexaCore Solutions, BrightMile Technologies, and Orion Digital Services are recommended for panel inclusion based on superior quality metrics and cooperative pricing behavior during Q2 renegotiations. Panelization is expected to concentrate 85% of FY2026 spend within contracted rate cards and standardized terms.

Section 4. Contracting Approach and Commercial Levers
All panel suppliers will operate under a unified Master Services Agreement (MSA) with harmonized liability caps, audit rights, and cybersecurity clauses. Rate cards will shift from time-and-materials dominance (currently 71% of spend) toward milestone-based and outcome-based pricing for project work, targeting a 12% reduction in blended day rates. Volume rebates of 2–4% will be triggered once annualized spend exceeds predefined thresholds per supplier. Additionally, gainshare provisions will be embedded in infrastructure optimization engagements to incentivize measurable cost take-out.

Section 5. FY2026 Savings and Risk Control Targets
The combined impact of supplier consolidation, internalization of Tier 1 SOC, and revised commercial constructs is forecast to deliver $4.1M in gross savings by the end of FY2026, equating to 8.4% of the current baseline. Risk exposure will be reduced through standardized data protection addenda, mandatory quarterly business reviews, and enhanced performance credit mechanisms tied to critical SLAs. Procurement and IT will jointly monitor savings realization via a quarterly benefits tracker reported to the Executive Finance Committee. Implementation of the preferred panel is scheduled to commence January 2026 with full transition by September 2026.

spec.title: IT Services Category Rationalization and Contracting Framework
spec.subtitle: Ref: SS-IT-2025-17 | Date: 22 September 2025 | From: Strategic Sourcing Office | To: CFO and CIO

sections.heading: 2025 Spend Baseline and Performance Overview
sections.body: Total FY2025 spend for the IT Services category reached $86.4M, representing 18.7% of total addressable indirect spend. The portfolio consists of application development ($31.2M), infrastructure and cloud operations ($27.5M), cybersecurity services ($12.8M), and end-user support and managed services ($14.9M). Spend is fragmented across 42 suppliers, with the top five vendors accounting for 61% of total outlay. Supplier performance data indicates schedule adherence averaging 83% and rate variance of +6.2% above benchmark in application development engagements.

sections.heading: Supplier Concentration and Risk Assessment
sections.body: A risk heatmap analysis identified over-dependence on two strategic integrators for critical cloud migration programs, exposing continuity and pricing leverage risks. Twelve suppliers generated less than $500K annually yet required full onboarding and compliance oversight, creating administrative inefficiencies. Three vendors failed to meet SLA uptime thresholds in Q2 and Q3 2025, triggering service credits totaling $740K. Rationalization to a preferred panel is expected to reduce operational risk and improve oversight consistency.

sections.heading: Make-versus-Buy Optimization
sections.body: 7 coverage requirements. The recommended model balances core capability ownership with external expertise for scalable and high-skill domains.

sections.heading: Preferred Supplier Panel Structure
sections.body: It is proposed to consolidate the supplier base to a panel of eight preferred providers: three strategic integrators, two cloud-managed service specialists, two cybersecurity firms, and one staff augmentation partner. Selection criteria include rate competitiveness (weighted 30%), delivery performance history (25%), technical certifications and capability depth (20%), risk and compliance maturity (15%), and innovation contribution (10%). Panel suppliers will be subject to quarterly business reviews and mandatory benchmarking against external rate indices. Non-panel engagements will require CIO and Procurement approval.

sections.heading: Contracting Approach and FY2026 Targets
sections.body: All preferred suppliers will transition to master services agreements incorporating standardized rate cards, gainshare mechanisms for productivity improvements, and capped annual rate escalations not exceeding CPI +1%. Outcome-based pricing will be piloted in two application modernization programs commencing Q1 FY2026. The sourcing initiative targets a minimum 8% addressable cost reduction, equivalent to $6.5M in annualized savings, while improving SLA compliance to 95% or greater. Implementation milestones include panel finalization by December 2025 and contract execution by March 2026.

spec.title: IT Services Category Rationalization and Contracting Framework FY2026
spec.subtitle: Ref: IT-STRAT-2025-17 | Date: 22 October 2025 | From: Strategic Sourcing Office

sections.heading: 2025 Spend Baseline and Performance Overview
sections.body: Total FY2025 IT Services spend closed at $86.4M, representing a 9.8% year-over-year increase driven primarily by cloud engineering support, cybersecurity incident response retainers, and ERP enhancement projects. The category is currently fragmented across 42 active suppliers, with the top 8 vendors accounting for 68% of total spend. Supplier performance data indicates average SLA attainment of 94.6%, though three mid-tier vendors recorded repeated schedule overruns exceeding 15% of contracted timelines. Rate benchmarking against industry quartiles shows that application development and DevOps resources are priced 6–11% above market median.

sections.heading: Category Segmentation and Demand Drivers
sections.body: Transformation Services. Growth in cybersecurity (up 22% YoY) reflects regulatory compliance requirements under the 2025 Data Resilience Directive and expanded threat monitoring scope. Infrastructure services show steady demand, while advisory spend is volatile and tied to discrete transformation initiatives. This segmentation supports targeted sourcing levers and differentiated contracting approaches.

sections.heading: Make-versus-Buy Assessment
sections.body: L2 infrastructure support, and standardized testing services will remain outsourced due to scale efficiencies and labor arbitrage benefits. The blended sourcing model is projected to reduce external run-rate spend by 12% while improving knowledge retention and operational control.

sections.heading: Preferred Supplier Panel Design
sections.body: The supplier base will be consolidated from 42 to a panel of 12 preferred partners by April 2026. Selection criteria weighted technical capability (30%), commercial competitiveness (25%), delivery performance history (20%), security posture (15%), and innovation capacity (10%). Strategic partners (maximum of four) will cover multi-tower managed services, while niche specialists will be retained for cybersecurity forensics and ERP optimization. Panel governance will include quarterly business reviews, standardized KPI dashboards, and mandatory continuous improvement commitments tied to gainshare incentives.

sections.heading: Contracting Approach and Risk Controls
sections.body: Future agreements will transition from time-and-materials structures toward outcome-based and milestone-linked pricing where scope stability permits. Master Services Agreements will include harmonized rate cards, productivity adjustment clauses, and benchmarking rights exercisable at 24-month intervals. Risk mitigation provisions include enhanced data protection schedules, step-in rights for critical services, and mandatory cyber liability coverage of not less than $10M per occurrence. Collectively, these measures are forecast to deliver $8.7M in cumulative cost reductions and measurable SLA improvement to 97% by the end of FY2026.
